vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2383: editable per-issue Standing Crew toggle on the issue view — upgrade PAN-2378's read-only chip

plan.title: feat(dashboard): editable per-issue Standing Crew toggle on the issue view — upgrade PAN-2378's read-only chip
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: The per-issue tiered-execution override already resolves (resolveTieredExecutionEnabled, tier-table.ts:124) and PAN-2378 shipped a READ-ONLY chip on the issue view (PlanCard.tsx:66-75). But there is no way to flip the override from the UI and no write door for it: the vBRIEF spec on main is immutable after planning (PAN-1124), so plan.metadata.tiered_execution cannot be edited in place. Operators can only set the override at planning time; they need to turn the Standing Crew on/off for a single issue AFTER planning.
narratives.Proposal: Give the per-issue override a mutable home in the per-issue record (.pan/records/<issue>.json), new field tieredExecutionOverride?: 'on'|'off' (unset = inherit), persisted through the existing writeRecord* write-door family. Extend resolveTieredExecutionEnabled so precedence is record override > plan.metadata.tiered_execution > global flag (fail-loud, no hardcoded fallback), add an issue-aware wrapper mirroring resolveReviewMode, thread it into dispatch, surface resolved effective state + source through the plan read door, add a PATCH write door, and make the issue-view chip an editable on/off/inherit control. Storage home is the record (not continue.json) because it is durable, git-traveling, and already the home for per-issue overrides that beat global config (reviewMode). Mid-flight flips affect subsequent dispatches only.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Editing the tier table / schema / dispatch behavior (PAN-1791 / PAN-2222 / PAN-2283 territory).
- Per-project tiered-execution editing or a per-project Settings surface (global Settings is PAN-2378's, unchanged).
- A second 'issue inspector' surface for the control — InspectorPanel is a defunct era (StatusHistoryTab.tsx:29); the canonical control lives in the cockpit PlanCard.tsx (the issue view).
- Mutating plan.metadata in place or writing to the vBRIEF spec file (PAN-1124); the inspection-policy PATCH's direct-spec-write is a structural template only, not the storage target.
- Retroactively re-dispatching or killing in-flight tier sessions on a flip (mid-flight = subsequent dispatches only).
- A pan CLI command for the override (UI toggle is the requirement; a CLI can follow later mirroring pan review mode).

autoDecisions.summary: Storage home = the per-issue record (.pan/records/<issue>.json), new field tieredExecutionOverride — not continue.json.
autoDecisions.rationale: Durable, travels with git, already the canonical home for per-issue overrides that beat global config (reviewMode). continue.json is workspace-scoped/ephemeral and its tierOverrides map is a different escalation concept. Matches the issue's candidate-#1 preference.

autoDecisions.summary: Single control surface = the cockpit PlanCard.tsx (issue view); no separate inspector bead.
autoDecisions.rationale: InspectorPanel is a defunct era (StatusHistoryTab.tsx:29 comment); no live inspector renders issue tiered state. Acceptance criterion #1 targets the issue view where the chip renders.

autoDecisions.summary: Read door computes precedence server-side and returns { effective, source, override }.
autoDecisions.rationale: Single-source-of-truth: the frontend stops computing precedence client-side; the resolver is the one read path for effective state.

autoDecisions.summary: Write door persists to the RECORD via writeRecord*, not to the spec file.
autoDecisions.rationale: The inspection-policy PATCH direct-spec-write is a structural template only; copying its storage target would violate PAN-1124 spec immutability.

autoDecisions.summary: Mid-flight = subsequent dispatches only; no kill/re-dispatch of in-flight tier sessions on a flip.
autoDecisions.rationale: Dispatch reads the record fresh at each spawn (mirroring resolveReviewMode); the PATCH mutates the record and returns without touching tmux/agents.
Avoids conflation with escalation's per-bead effective-difficulty tierOverrides map (tier-replay.ts:60).

autoDecisions.summary: This issue dogfoods the override: plan.metadata.tiered_execution = 'on'.
autoDecisions.rationale: Operator mandate (RUN-56): PAN-2383 is built BY the Standing Crew via the per-issue override, exercising all three tiers + escalation on film.

items.title: Record-backed override home + resolver precedence extension

expected_outputs: per-issue-tier-override.test.ts passes including new record-precedence cases
metadata.readinessReason: Foundation bead runs first in wave 0; no sibling touches record.ts or tier-table.ts, so it is parallel-safe by construction.

narrative.Action: Add a mutable per-issue override field tieredExecutionOverride?: 'on' | 'off' to interface PanIssueRecord in src/lib/pan-dir/record.ts (next to reviewMode at :139, unset = inherit). Add write-door setters writeRecordTieredExecutionOverrideSync (+ async) modeled on writeRecordScopeDriftSync (record.ts:607: ensureIssueRecordSync -> mutate field -> writeIssueRecordSync -> queueIssueRecordCommit); passing null/undefined clears the field (back to inherit). Extend resolveTieredExecutionEnabled (tier-table.ts:124) to accept the record override with precedence record override > planMetadata.tiered_execution > config.enabled — reuse the existing 'on'/'off'/throw fail-loud logic for the record value; unset record override must preserve today's behavior byte-for-byte. Add an issue-aware wrapper resolveTieredExecutionEnabledForIssue(issueId, planMetadata) that reads the record via readIssueRecordSync (mirroring resolveReviewMode at review-agent.ts:890) and calls the extended core. Extend per-issue-tier-override.test.ts with the record-precedence matrix. Foundation: dispatch-wiring, api-read-door, and api-write-door all encode assumptions about this field name, value domain, and precedence.

items.title: PanIssueRecord exposes tieredExecutionOverride?: 'on' | 'off'; the new writeRecord* setter persists it and queues the record auto-commit; passing null clears it back to inherit

resolveTieredExecutionEnabled returns the record override when set ('on'->true, 'off'->false) regardless of plan-metadata or global flag; when record override is unset it returns exactly the pre-existing plan-metadata>global result
An invalid stored override value throws TieredExecutionConfigError rather than silently inheriting (fail-loud, no hardcoded fallback)

resolveTieredExecutionEnabledForIssue reads the per-issue record via readIssueRecordSync and applies record>plan-metadata>global; per-issue-tier-override.test.ts passes with the added record-precedence cases
Honor the record override in live agent dispatch

expected_outputs: dispatch-record-override.test.ts asserts the record override flips the resolved enabled state on the next spawn

narrative.Action: Thread the issue id + record override into the two dispatch functions in src/lib/agents/spawn-prep.ts — resolveSlotTierSpawnParams (:211-236, resolve call :225) and resolveSingleWorkTierSpawnParams (:246-265, resolve call :257) — so live dispatch honors the record override on the next spawn. These functions currently receive workspace/baseWorkspace but not the issue id; derive or pass it (the issue id is recoverable from the workspace path / plan doc) and call resolveTieredExecutionEnabledForIssue instead of the bare resolver. Apply the same issue-aware resolution at the other issue-scoped call sites for consistency: dispatch-tier.ts:66, cloister/inspect-agent.ts:156, routes/tiered-inspect-escalation.ts:51, routes/tiered-callouts.ts:137. Add/extend a dispatch unit test proving a record override 'off' disables tiered dispatch even when global+plan-metadata say on (and vice-versa).

items.title: Both spawn-prep dispatch functions resolve tiered-enabled via the issue-aware resolver so a record override 'off' disables tiered dispatch on the next spawn even when the global flag and plan-metadata are 'on'
A record override 'on' enables tiered dispatch on the next spawn even when the global flag is off, matching resolveTieredExecutionEnabledForIssue

For a given record override, the inspect-agent, tiered-inspect-escalation, and tiered-callouts paths each return the same effective enabled value as the dispatch path (a test flips the override and asserts all sites agree)
Plan read door returns resolved tieredExecution block

expected_outputs: tiered-execution-route.test.ts asserts the tieredExecution block with correct source for record-override / plan-metadata / global cases

narrative.Action: Extend getWorkspacePlanRoute (GET /api/workspaces/:issueId/plan, src/dashboard/server/routes/workspaces/workspace-data.ts:763-786) so its JSON response includes a computed tieredExecution: { effective: boolean, source: 'issue-override' | 'plan-metadata' | 'global', override: 'on' | 'off' | null } block. Compute effective via resolveTieredExecutionEnabledForIssue(issueId, plan.metadata) with the global tieredExecution config; compute source by precedence: record override set -> 'issue-override'; else plan.metadata.tiered_execution set -> 'plan-metadata'; else 'global'; override = the raw record value or null. Keep the existing spread response shape intact (additive field). Add a route test covering all three source cases.

items.title: GET /api/workspaces/:issueId/plan returns a tieredExecution { effective, source, override } object alongside the existing plan doc fields
The response returns source 'issue-override' when a record override is set, 'plan-metadata' when only plan.metadata.tiered_execution is set, and 'global' when neither is set
The response returns effective equal to resolveTieredExecutionEnabledForIssue for the issue and override equal to the raw record value or null
PATCH write door persists the override to the record

expected_outputs: tiered-execution-route.test.ts asserts persist round-trip, 400 on invalid input, and that no agent is signalled

narrative.Action: Add a new route patchWorkspaceTieredExecutionRoute = PATCH /api/workspaces/:issueId/tiered-execution, mirroring the structure of patchWorkspacePlanInspectionPolicyRoute (workspace-data.ts:822-870): requireTrustedMutationOrigin(request) first, parseIssueIdSync, readJsonBody, then validate body.override against the allow-list 'on' | 'off' | null (400 'Invalid tiered-execution override' otherwise). Persist via the writeRecordTieredExecutionOverride setter from design-override-home (null clears -> inherit) — NOT by writing the spec file. Return the updated computed tieredExecution block (same shape as the read door). Register the route in the workspaceDataRouteLayer Layer.mergeAll list (:917-925). The handler must NOT signal, kill, or resume any agent (mid-flight = subsequent dispatches only). Add a route test: valid persist round-trip, invalid value -> 400, and an assertion that no agent lifecycle call is made.

items.title: PATCH /api/workspaces/:issueId/tiered-execution with { override: 'on' | 'off' | null } persists via the record write door and returns the updated tieredExecution block
The PATCH rejects an override value outside 'on' | 'off' | null with HTTP 400 and preserves the existing record (no mutation)
A persisted override survives a fresh read (round-trip via readIssueRecordSync / the read door) and the handler makes no agent lifecycle call (no kill/signal/resume)
A PATCH without a trusted mutation origin returns the origin-error response, while a valid PATCH through the registered route returns HTTP 200
